messages:
alex k: small thread: on REST vs gRPC discussion, one blocker for app teams is the canary routing granularity. If gateway strips proto labels, we lose per-model canary.

nina: yeah. we run gRPC for internal but external browsers hit json. We need a consistent routing key exposed to the router. Suggest a header shim that is always present.

ben: Implementation note: envoy transcoder exists but we currently don't use it due to performance. The shim is cheaper: map proto labels -> headers in an interceptor.

ci-bot: build passed: gateway-transcode-shim v2. PR #4521 green.

ryan: Ops question: will this change affect our quota metering pipeline? metric ingestion wants a stable key. Also how will we handle legacy clients?

alex k: meter pipeline will accept header-based routing key `rw-routing-key`. For legacy clients, default to tenant header in auth token.

nina: Add `rw-routing-v=2` so we can iterate the format. Also we should include a signature header `rw-routing-sig` to avoid header spoofing.

ben: signature seems heavy. simpler: gateway overwrites any incoming `rw-routing-key` and logs mismatch -> increments `gateway.routing.overrides`.

ryan: agreed. Also add a canary dashboard filter so SREs can drill into translated vs native requests.

alex k: ok I'll file RFC and schedule 2% canary next week.
